title: OneDrive: pay-as-you-go storage beyond licensed quotas
summary: The billing model, published price, prerequisites and rollout statements are supported. The assertion that content-access permissions remain unchanged is not documented, and several correct navigation paths stop short of the actual setting.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a new consumption-based meter for additional OneDrive storage for selected accounts beyond licensed limits.
claims.quote: New pay-as-you-go, consumption-based meter for additional OneDrive storage. Control which OneDrive accounts can grow beyond their licensed storage limits and give selected users more space as needed.

claims.claim: The licensing model is consumption-based pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 OneDrive Storage is a pay-as-you-go service that provides flexible billing to add storage to your OneDrive accounts.

claims.claim: The service can be connected at Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Services > Connect a policy.
claims.quote: go to Billing > Pay-as-you-go. On the Pay-as-you-go page, select the Services tab. For the service that you want to connect, in the Billing policy column, select Connect a policy.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and the matching table path to 'Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Services > Connect a policy > policy > Connection status'. The cited page says to find the policy in the side panel and set its Connection status toggle to Connected.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation is documented for connecting or disconnecting this OneDrive Storage billing service.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 OneDrive Storage" "connect" "API"; "Microsoft 365" "billing policies" "API" "OneDrive". Read Billing-node setup and Graph OneDrive/Backup API search excerpts; no applicable operation found.

claims.claim: Disconnecting the service uses the Connection status toggle.
claims.quote: In the side panel, select the Billing policies tab. In the Connection status column, select the Connected toggle to turn it off.

claims.claim: The per-user control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > OneDrive > Storage used > Edit.
claims.quote: expand Users and select Active users. Select the user whose storage you want to change. Go to the OneDrive tab. Under Storage used, select Edit. Choose the Maximum storage for this user option and set the storage limit.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and the matching table path to 'Users > Active users > user > OneDrive > Storage used > Edit > Maximum storage for this user'. The existing path reaches the correct pane but stops before the option already named in the note.

claims.claim: When Microsoft 365 OneDrive Storage is enabled, the per-user storage limit may exceed the user's licensed storage.
claims.quote: If your tenant has Microsoft 365 OneDrive Storage enabled, you can set a user's OneDrive storage limit higher than the storage included with their license.

claims.claim: The setting is named Maximum storage for this user.
claims.quote: Choose the Maximum storage for this user option and set the storage limit.

claims.claim: Budget preferences are at Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Pay-as-you-go > policy > Budget > Settings.
claims.quote: go to Billing > Pay-as-you-go. On the Pay-as-you-go page, select the policy that you want to manage. In the policy panel, select the Budget tab. To configure your budget and alert preferences, select Settings.
claims.fix: Extend controls[2].ui.path and the matching table path to 'Billing > Pay-as-you-go > policy > Budget > Settings > Send email alerts > Add more' for the spending-alert threshold control. The cited page places additional alert thresholds under Send email alerts.
